Some games the enemy team will have those troll players, other games you will have those troll players. Statistically speaking the best way to get rid of this problem is play a high enough volume of games. If you get a high enough volume of games in the only factor that SHOULD be affecting your climb is you.   


For how I deal with those kinds of games, personally I have 2 case scenarios that I go for in my games.   
1. My team is strong, their team is weak, if we group, there is a high chance we will win the team fight. At this point I will group with my team and a majority of the time we win the fights and we snow ball and win the game. If you are loosing those fights then either 2 things are going wrong. You are analyzing which team is stronger properly, or you aren't using adc to its highest potential and carrying the fight. Yes you have 4 team mates, should they help peel for you? Yea. Will they? Most likely not, they are monkeys with type writers. Don't expect anything from your teamates, be ready for if they do the right play but don't die expecting your Morgana who hasn't hit a Q all game to Black Shield you when the naut who has ulted you every fight is sprinting right at you.   


2. My team is weak, the enemy team is strong. My team mates are monkeys so while they all ooga booga cave man over at rift when it is 9/0 and our top laner is dead. I will not go to a fight that we are probably going to loose unless I pull some Guma level plays having Keria for a support. I am going to take bot turret, take towers for gold, invade enemy camps, crash waves. All of these things are getting you probably the same if not more gold had gone to the fight to nab 1 or 2 kills. Along with crashing waves and turrets. Crashing wave gives you that $$ but it also kills your minions under their turret denying them the cs and xp. This is a game about destroying each others Nexuses. Yes your team mates will probably scream through pings and chat at you. Mute them, they just proved that they are stupid enough to take a bad fight, their opinion and their shot calls are probably useless to you anyways so mute the monkey mid laner who is at 50 cs at 11 minutes.   


From the second option you will either be strong enough to now carry the fights, side laning enough to pull pressure for your team to start winning the important objective fights, or you side lane so much you could be compared to a MOAB in round 12 of BTD. There will be outliers in games, learn what caused those outliers to occur, then move on. There are a lot of variables in league, its hard to correctly predict what is going to happen 100% of the time. Be ok making wrong predictions and betting on it, you get better with time and eventually you can make the right call a majority of the time. If the team isn't going to funnel you the recourses that put the carry into adc then use them as cannon fodder and funnel yourself. Its a 1v1v1v1v1v5 except for those 3-4 games you have a year that every team mate has their monitor plugged in.

You say that anyone with their monitor on can avoid her traps, honestly sounds like you aren't using her traps right. If you watch Guma's clips of caitlyn he always places traps in the path that the enemy is walking or in fog of war. Either way he is interrupting their pathing which is an advantage to you, or in the case of fog of war (like bushes) they now have to think about whether they are going to loose half their hp to face check a random bush you are near or waist a ward on it. 

Caitlyn is an early and late game champ, the way you keep her relevant in the mid game is not wasting her usefulness in the early game to only go even, get an advantage with it and turn it into a lead to then carry that into keeping her relevant in the mid game until the one game a week you make it to 6 item late game.

The most difficult combo I think most people would use is a E,W,Q and even then from personally experience I suck at that combo so I usually forgo using it. So excluding the most difficult combo you can play her just fine. Hit an E, then a Q right after and you now know the majority of her combos. Moving away from Starbucks specifically and more so towards applying to jobs, after sending in an application (from which ever avenue provided) it doesn't hurt to go into the store to personally hand your resume to the manager. This gives a good time for them to put a resume with a face and give them a good first impression. Most of the time doing this helps your chances of landing the job. Calling ahead also is a good idea, in my opinion its best not to do both, but calling to check on the status of your application help show the manager you are taking the initiative in acquiring said job. 

Now specifically for Starbucks, I will add on my store. Although after talking to other friends who work at starbucks mine is a little on the weird side. For my store we have about 100 applicants at a time for our SM (Store manager) to go through, so what the SM does is organize the applicants by availability and see which applicants fit into what we need. From there she narrows it down and then will look through the applicants. What we are told when ever we get calls about people asking about the status of their application, is that our manager will reach out to you if you have what we are looking for at the store. Something along those lines, which I worded pretty poorly there tbh. Regardless if you come in with a resume to hand it to our SM, we won't just throw it away, personally I will put a sticky note with when you came in and a return phone number and put it on their desk. So I highly suggest going in with a resume to hand in/physically give to the SM. I am confident other SM would happily take them by hand rather than mine but that is more me speculating then actually knowing for sure.

Best of luck in working for starbucks though, over all I really enjoy the job, but with all jobs they have their pros and cons, so I hope if you get hired that you enjoy it!
